analysis.title: Marketcolour + Nvidia / Whitbread / Prysmian / Banks
key_insights: US equities fell for a further session on 18 Nov 2026: SPX -103bps to 7340 with all 11 sectors down, VIX above 25, and the S&P 500 below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April. Financials -1.87%, Utilities -1.60%.
NDX fell 72bps to 27001 and RTY fell 150bps to 2701. The GS High Beta Momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) rose 1.92% and the GS Momentum Hi/Lo basket (GSP1MOMO) rose 1.67%, both outperforming.
In Europe, SXXP fell 1.8%, its worst day since March, with 92% of stocks closing lower. EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) fell 2.9% and Software (GSSBSFTW) fell 4.4%.

Nvidia said on its call that token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May, which has accelerated token usage and demand for compute. GPU rental prices are rising across generations: Hopper GPUs re-contracted at up to twice their original price under multi-year agreements, and B300 rates are up more than 60% since introduction.

Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8bn vs consensus $109.5bn, gross margin of 74.9% vs consensus 73.5%, and data center revenue of $107.6bn vs consensus $102.0bn. Management raised its CY27 revenue growth forecast to +75% from +70%. Rubin generated $20bn of revenue in its first quarter. Financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners are $518bn. GS rates it Buy with a $220 price target (40% upside, 8.6x PE 2028E). Investor positioning going in was neutral to negative.

Nike's investor day was not enough for GS. Management sees FY29 as the turning point and still expects sales to fall by high single digits in FY2027 as it cuts Sportswear and Jordan supply and resets its China business.

Whitbread: GS expects PBT to grow at a 14% CAGR over FY27-31E and ROCE to expand by about 680bps by FY31E vs FY27E. Shareholder returns are expected to improve sooner than the market expects, with scope to begin buybacks next year. Shares trade near their lowest multiple of the last 10+ years. Rated 'Up to Buy' with a GBP37 target (32% upside).

Prysmian: GS raised FY26-28E adjusted EBITDA by about 2-3% after the 3Q26 beat. It sees Prysmian above the top end of 2026 EBITDA guidance and expects 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance above EUR4bn at full-year results. Buy, EUR174 target (60% upside).

Eurobank announced the acquisition of 65% of Bulgarian bank Fibank, worth EUR1bn for 100%, financed from excess capital plus a EUR750m ABB (4% of market cap). GS sees 7% EPS accretion, 12% PAT accretion pro forma for the share capital increase, and 21% return on consumed capital pro forma.

BNP's BNL deep dive set new 2030 targets: revenue growth above 3% vs consensus 2.4%, NII growth of 2.5%, fee growth of 4%, cost/income of 56% vs consensus 57%, and risk-weighted assets down 0.5% CAGR vs consensus up.

Smiths Group 1Q organic revenue was 0%, light vs whispers of about 3%. A slow start had been expected. The company kept its FY guide of about 4% organic growth, with acceleration through the year (John Crane weighted to H2, Flex-Tek to H1) after Middle East disruption affected John Crane.

market_movers.rationale: Revenue, gross margin and data center revenue all beat consensus, and management raised its CY27 growth forecast to 75% from 70%. Rubin is ramping fastest in company history.
Whitbread's earnings, returns on capital and shareholder returns are set to improve sooner than the market expects, while the shares trade near a 10+ year trough multiple. Rated 'Up to Buy'.
Prysmian's FY26-28E adjusted EBITDA estimates were raised by 2-3% after the 3Q26 beat. GS expects results above the top end of 2026 guidance.
